geometry_edits.rationale: Add a sectionally expressive support layer on top of the current root to strengthen roof/section fit for neighborhood living.
Folded section gives a legible inhabited roof profile and avoids an over-generic flat or boxy top.
Keep the profile aligned to the long bar direction so the dominant mass remains readable in all views.
Slightly enlarge the courtyard/opening to improve publicness and ground-level usability.

graph_edits.rationale: Wrap the current composed mass with a sectionally legible roof/upper profile so the silhouette reads as inhabited and civic rather than generic box-plus-courtyard.
A folded family adds clear section logic compatible with neighborhood public/program hierarchy without turning the mass into a hall or tower.
Preserve the long horizontal neighborhood-scale reading and align the roof expression with the bar-like dominant mass.
Slightly enlarge the void so the public threshold becomes more usable and less like a thin subtraction.

rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent early-stage neighborhood-living massing with one dominant bent/looped bar and a meaningful carved courtyard/void. It responds reasonably to the parcel rather than merely filling a box, and the blue frontage is met by a legible open/entry seam rather than a sealed edge. Across the four views the form remains consistent, with no obvious cross-view volume collisions. The silhouette is somewhat stepped but not irresponsibly fragmented; the main weakness is that the section is still fairly generic and could better express an inhabited roof/terrace or clearer ground-public sequence. Overall it is program-fit for compact mixed neighborhood use because it supports an active threshold, public void, and upper mass hierarchy without drifting into tower or hall typology.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more pavilion-like and sculptural than the candidate; avoid copying its scalloped roof expression.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Curved/ordered low-rise massing with a large central void and bridge-like connector; good precedent for a compact public threshold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much larger and more multi-building than the candidate; use only the courtyard-and-hierarchy principle.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/campus-like composition around a central plaza; supports neighborhood-scale mixed public space.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Its facade openness and greenhouse-like roof are not required here.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Elongated low-rise mass with a carved central void and strong horizontal spread; useful for active-ground / public-inset logic.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More complex and landscape-dominant than the candidate; don’t over-fragment into campus pieces.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Spread-out interconnected wings and terraced connections can produce a legible civic sequence without fragmenting the mass.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is more rectilinear and layered; the candidate should keep its own bent-bar character.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking volumes with a clear central void and elevated connections; reinforces hierarchy and public interior-exterior transition.

warnings: The mass is coherent, but the section still feels a little under-articulated for a strong neighborhood-living brief.
The stepped/roof articulation is acceptable but not yet distinctive enough to become the main spatial idea.
Public void is legible, but could be made more obviously usable and not just subtractive.
